title: Pi: The Circle Number
summary: Why every circle has the same secret ratio, about 3.14.

steps.title: Circles and rulers
sentences: Take any circle and measure around its edge, called the circumference.
Now measure across the middle, called the diameter.
Divide the first by the second and you always get a number a little more than 3.
points: Their ratio is always the same

steps.title: Meet pi
sentences: That number is called pi, written with the Greek letter π.
It is about 3.14159, and its digits go on forever without repeating.
So the circumference of a circle is pi times its diameter.

steps.title: Using pi
sentences: The area of a circle is pi times the radius times the radius.
If a circle has a radius of 7 centimetres, its area is about 154 square centimetres.
At school we often use 22 over 7 or 3.14 for pi.

steps.title: A long chase
sentences: Ancient people such as the Egyptians and Babylonians found rough values of pi.
Indian mathematician Madhava of Sangamagrama found a series to calculate it in the 1300s.
Today computers have worked out trillions of its digits, and 14 March is celebrated as Pi Day.

facts: Because pi has no end, 22/7 is only a close fraction, not exactly pi.
Pi appears in many places in science, not just circles, such as waves and the shape of rivers.
NASA uses only about 15 digits of pi for its space calculations.

quiz.q: Pi is the ratio of the circumference to the...
quiz.why: Circumference divided by diameter equals pi.
